name: Rebrending
description: Kostya and Zhenya — the creators of the band "Paper" — after the release of the legendary album decided to create a new band "Day movers", for this they need to find two new people. They invited $$$n$$$ people to the casting. The casting will last $$$q$$$ days. On the $$$i$$$th of the days, Kostya and Zhenya want to find two people on the segment from $$$l_i$$$ to $$$r_i$$$ who are most suitable for their band. Since "Day movers" are doing a modern art, musical skills are not important to them and they look only at other signs: they want the height difference between two people to be as small as possible. Help them, and for each day, find the minimum difference in the growth of people from the casting on this segment!
input_specification: In the first line you are given two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5, 1 \leq q \leq 10^6$$$) — the number of people who came to the casting and the number of casting days. In the second line, you are given $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) — the growth of each of the candidates. It is also guaranteed that all $$$a_i$$$ are different . The following $$$q$$$ lines each contains two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq l_i \lt r_i \leq n$$$) — a segment of people on the $$$i$$$th day of casting.
output_specification: Output $$$q$$$ lines. In the $$$i$$$-th line there should be a minimum height difference between the two candidates on the segment on the $$$i$$$-th day of casting.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1793F — Rebrending [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
